source.title: Defeating Cerberus: Concept-Guided Privacy-Leakage Mitigation in Multimodal Language Models
source.authors: Boyang Zhang; I. E. Akkus; Ruichuan Chen; Alice Dethise; Klaus Satzke; Ivica Rimac; Yang Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study cites single-direction refusal work as background but develops and evaluates a different intervention: steering a composite PII-sensitivity concept. It does not test the claimed harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction or its ablation.
record.gate_note: The reported steering results concern the study's own PII concept, not the refusal direction in the claim; they are recorded as fits_no_version. Concept-extraction accuracies are used to select steering layers and are not included. Baseline methods in Table 1 are not included because they are comparisons for the study's own method, not tests of the claimed direction.
record.test_reason: The study steers a PCA-derived composite PII-sensitivity concept (PII vs non-PII statements), added to backbone weights of VLMs, and reports only its own method's refusal rates against prompt-based baselines. It cites Arditi et al. as inspiration but never extracts the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, ablates it, or tests any version of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that concept-steering of backbone LLM weights gives an average refusal rate of 93.3% on PII tasks, with minimal impact on unrelated tasks. They add that it beats prompt-based baselines and needs no retraining or fine-tuning.
record.recipe_differences: The study extracts a composite PII-and-sensitivity concept using PCA over paired PII/non-PII activations, then adds it to selected backbone weights. It does not extract the claimed harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction or ablate it at every layer and position. The tested goal is PII leakage mitigation.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that later layers extract the PII concept more accurately, select layers for steering, and show that steering coefficient affects both PII refusal and benign-task performance. For Mistral-7B, they describe a gap around coefficients 0.4 to 0.6 between mitigation decline and benign-task disruption. Simulated scan artifacts and PII type also change outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding a PCA-derived PII-sensitivity concept vector to selected later-layer backbone weights raises refusal on PII-extraction image tasks from near 0 to 0.85–1.0 (r1–r36). Refusal on non-PII tasks stays low (0–0.065). Results depend on the steering coefficient, and email and phone requests are refused less often than address requests.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A PII-sensitivity concept direction, added to VLM backbone weights, induces targeted refusal of PII-extraction requests with little refusal on unrelated tasks.

record.code_released: The authors say they will open-source the dataset-generation and mitigation code; no URL is stated.
record.problems: The study measures refusal using searches for typical refusal phrases and counts nonsensical outputs as refusals; it explicitly does not evaluate OCR performance. Results are averages over 5 runs, but error bars are omitted. The text's description of Vicuna-7B email mitigation (35%) conflicts with the apparent Table 4 value (0.791). The authors report that MiniGPT-4 and Llava were excluded from the main evaluation because of poor image-text extraction and hallucination.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 comparison-baseline values were left out because they compare other defenses rather than test the claimed direction. Section 5.2 and Figures 3–5 report concept-extraction accuracies and projections used to choose layers or visualize separation; these do not test the claimed refusal direction. Figure 6's coefficient sweep is described qualitatively but its plotted values are not extracted as separate rows.

untested.parts: All: no harmful-minus-harmless direction, no ablation, no addition of a refusal direction.
All: the weight edit adds a PII concept to induce refusal; no abliteration.
All. The 2-PC visualisation concerns the PII concept, not refusal.
All: applying the method across backbones is not transfer of the refusal direction.

record.verdict_notes: Refusal is detected by phrase matching, and nonsensical outputs count as refusals. The unsteered refusal rate on DocVQA and on PII-type subsets is not reported. This is a T4/T6-adjacent use of the steering idea; none of V1–V8 is tested.

versions.untested_parts: The claimed harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, its removal, refusal of harmless requests after adding it, and preservation of general capability after its ablation.
No weight edit removing the claimed refusal direction in released models.
No test of attacks suppressing the claimed direction or training against its ablation.
No test of whether refusal is affine, cone-shaped, or distributed across a dominant direction and other directions.
No separation test of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
The study applies its own PII steering method to several model backbones, but does not test transfer of the claimed refusal direction across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models.
No comparison of refusal training methods or stages.
